question: Which nanocarriers for siRNA delivery are shown under the metal-based nanoparticles heading?
expect: AuNPs, SPIONs and MOF (figure reading, OCR-confirmed)

Document: "Engineered nanomaterials for siRNA therapy against tumor metastasis"

Page 8, Section: "4.1.4. Metal nanoparticles"

Metal nanoparticles, derived from metal-containing compounds, constitute a class of nanomaterials that incorporate metal ions and are often conjugated with various inorganic or organic molecules [90].
A broad range of metal nanoparticles has been developed, such as gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), iron oxide and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), have become important nanoplat-forms for the passive targeted delivery of siRNA owing to their controllable size, stable structure, and diverse functionalities [94].
AuNPs have attracted significant attention as metal nanocarriers owing to their favorable physicochemical properties.

The cisplatin loading efficiency reaches 43.41% ±11.12%, effectively protecting and delivering siVEGF and THPP.
Overall, metal nanoparticles serve as effective siRNA delivery vehi-cles due to their high specific surface area, which enables efficient drug loading.

The cisplatin loading efficiency is computed as a percentage of 43.41% ±11.12%
